en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Eleventh Chapter
Is impermanence fully established? Yes.
Is impermanence fully established by that very impermanence?
One should not say so … [as before] … Is impermanence fully established by that very impermanence?
[Opponent: Yes.
[Proponent: By that very [path], there is no making an end of suffering, no cutting off of the round of existence, and no parinibbāna through non-clinging?
You should not say so.
Is aging fully accomplished? Yes.
Is aging fully accomplished by that aging? No.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is aging fully established by that aging? Yes.
By that very [state], is there no making an end of suffering, no cutting off of the round of existence, and no final Nibbāna through non-clinging?
One should not say so...
Is death an accomplished reality?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Is the death of that death fully established?
You should not say so.
Is that death the death of that [death] which is fully accomplished? Yes.
Then, for that very [death], is there no making an end of suffering, no cutting off of the cycle of existence, and no final Nibbāna through non-clinging?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is matter fully established, and is there impermanence of matter? Yes.
Is impermanence fully established? Is there impermanence of impermanence?
One should not say so...
[and so on] ...Is form fully established? Is there aging of form?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Is aging fully accomplished? Is there aging of aging?
You should not speak thus … [and so on] … .
Is form fully accomplished; is there the breaking up of form; is there the disappearance of form?
Yes. Is death fully accomplished; is there the breaking up of death; is there the disappearance of death? Yes.
It should not be said so … [as before] … Feeling … perception … mental formations … [as before] …
Is consciousness fully accomplished, and does the impermanence of consciousness exist? Yes.
Is impermanence fully accomplished, and does the impermanence of impermanence exist?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Consciousness is fully established; does aging exist for consciousness? Yes.
Is aging fully established? Is there the disintegration of aging? Is there the disappearance of aging?
One should not say so… [as before] … Is consciousness fully established?
Is there the breaking up of consciousness? Is there the disappearance of consciousness?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Is death fully established; is there a dissolution of death; is there its disappearance?
You should not say so …pe… [as before].
The Discussion on Impermanence is finished.
The eleventh chapter.
Its summary verse:

The underlying tendencies (*anusaya*) are indeterminate (*abyākata*), rootless (*ahetuka*), dissociated from consciousness (*cittavippayutta*); when ignorance has vanished, one possesses knowledge; knowledge is dissociated from consciousness;
where knowledge regarding sounds occurs, one endowed with the power of psychic success (*iddhibala*) might remain for an eon (*kappa*);
the continuity of mind is concentration (*samādhi*); the stability of phenomena (*dhammaṭṭhitatā*); and impermanence (*aniccatā*).
